heroLead: West Newton sits along the Youghiogheny River in southern Westmoreland County, close to some of the busiest Marcellus development in the region.
intro: We've noticed something about river towns like West Newton: the families holding mineral rights here tend to also hold a lot of institutional memory about the land, who leased first, which company came through, what the neighbors got paid. That kind of local knowledge is useful, but it's not the same as knowing what your specific interest is worth today.
That's the gap we try to close, honestly and without a sales pitch attached.

sections.heading: Southern Westmoreland's Position in the Play
paragraphs: West Newton sits closer to the Washington and Fayette county line, where the Marcellus wet gas fairway runs strongest, than to the more moderate northern half of Westmoreland County. That positioning matters because liquids-rich gas typically brings higher wellhead value than dry gas, which can translate into stronger royalty checks when production and deductions are accounted for correctly.
We check where your unit actually sits relative to that fairway rather than assuming a county-wide average applies to your parcel.

sections.heading: The Kilmer Decision and Why It Still Matters
paragraphs: Pennsylvania's Kilmer v. Elexco Land Services decision upheld an operator's right to deduct post-production costs from royalty payments as long as the lease language allowed it and the check stayed above the one-eighth statutory floor. That ruling shaped how most Marcellus-era leases in Westmoreland County are enforced today, and it's a big part of why so many owners near West Newton have watched their checks shrink over the life of a well.
We're not attorneys and this isn't legal advice, but understanding that background helps explain why a lease that looked fair when it was signed can produce a disappointing check years later.

sections.heading: What We'll Actually Offer
paragraphs: We calculate an offer based on your confirmed net mineral acreage, your unit's production trend, and current market conditions, not a flat per-acre number pulled from a chart. Every West Newton interest we've looked at has been different enough that a generic number wouldn't be honest.

faqs.question: What was the Kilmer v. Elexco case about?
faqs.answer: It's a Pennsylvania court decision that upheld post-production cost deductions from royalties when lease language permits them, as long as the payment stays above the statutory one-eighth floor.
